chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Buy an animal, for its benefit is for you and its sustenance is upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.دَابَّة: Animal, riding beast — refers especially to a riding animal or mount used for transport
key_terms.رِزْق: Sustenance, provision — used in Islamic theology to denote provision that comes from God
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — a common honorific formula for God
key_terms.مَنْفَعَة: Benefit, utility, advantage — refers to the practical use one gets from the animal

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about buying a riding animal and its sustenance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) encourages acquiring a riding animal, offering a practical economic rationale: its utility belongs to the owner while the responsibility for its provision rests with God. This teaching reflects the Islamic concept of tawakkul (reliance on God), particularly as it relates to the livelihoods of animals — the Quran affirms that there is no creature on earth but that God provides for it (11:6). The hadith gently motivates a hesitant person (perhaps deterred by the cost of feeding an animal) by assuring them that God undertakes sustenance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Raib who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Buy an animal, for its benefit would be for you and its sustenance would be upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ali ibn Ri’ab who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Buy a stumper; its benefit is for you and its sustenance with Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’”
